Coauthored exhibits to retain
- Sol's G19 successive-owner figure connects the same group's ownership, expenditure and receipts.
It is the preferred concrete economic timeline in the main text. - Sol's spending-window comparison explains why whole-game receipts differ from post-own-expenditure receipts.

The Sol manifest includes the all-103-unit cross-check. - Sol's alternative outcome grid and Opus's grid remain alternatives, not additional independent datasets. - Fable's house-stock grid, series and report reconstruct bank inventory at all 6,989 delivered states.
Hotel conversions return houses and produce upward steps.
Zero stock is not a count of denied demand. - Fable's all-63 first-management table distinguishes built, never legal, defaults, received conflicts and valid ENDs.
Sol's follow-up check recounts the derived rows with attribution. - Normative contracts, implemented/measured/proposed affordances and cost/usage support methods and discussion.
Known cost has missing refusal accounting; token semantics differ by provider.
Draft selection
The venue-neutral draft should give economics and social conduct substantial space.
Use F1/F2 for interpretation and design, F3/F4 for negotiation/deployment, F5 plus the G19 timeline for receipts and inheritance, F6 for finance, and F8 for social contrasts.
F7 can be a table beside deployment.
F9, stock trajectories and the alternative plots can move to an appendix without losing their evidence.
Do not remove the condition/default annotations merely to simplify a plot.
Do not replace all-player trajectories with winner-only anecdotes.
Final numbering and layout will be chosen during the manuscript stage, after the prose and exhibits are placed together.
